title: The four Labour Codes: a plain-language map
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Twenty-nine central laws were folded into four Codes. Here is what each one covers.
body:
Parliament passed four Labour Codes in 2019 and 2020, merging 29 central labour laws into four. Anyone who works with labour questions should know what each Code is about.

## The four Codes

- **Code on Wages, 2019:** minimum wages, timely payment of wages, bonus and equal remuneration. It replaces four older laws, including the Minimum Wages Act and the Payment of Wages Act.
- **Industrial Relations Code, 2020:** trade unions, standing orders, lay-off, retrenchment, closure and strikes. It replaces the Trade Unions Act, the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act and the Industrial Disputes Act.
- **Code on Social Security, 2020:** provident fund, ESI, gratuity, maternity benefit and, for the first time, a framework for gig and platform workers. It replaces nine social security laws.
- **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020:** safety, health and working conditions in factories, mines, docks, building work and other establishments.

## Why one law each?

The older laws had different definitions of "employee", "wages" and "establishment". The aim of the Codes is uniform definitions, fewer registrations and returns, and wider coverage.

## BMS's position

BMS has said that it welcomes the simplification and the extension of social security, but has also argued, in consultation with the Government, that some provisions need to change so that workers' rights are not diluted. This blog will look at those questions in later posts.
